name: Deep Aqua
lede: Deep Aqua is a dark, muted teal, a darkened step from the web color Aqua that Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates earlier than Ridgway's own 1912 plate.

sections.title: Two dictionaries, two dates
sections.body: Ridgway plotted Deep Aqua in 1912, on plate VII, hue 41, tone i [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary lists it too, giving it an earlier first-recorded date of 1905, on plate 36 K 1 [2]. The name darkens [[aqua]], the web color that is itself a shortened form of the Latin for water [3]. Two other names in our library sit close enough in color to count as near-duplicates, Water Blue and Ethyl Green, though the ISCC-NBS 1955 blocks that go with those two names are not Deep Aqua's own filing [2]. Its nearest named neighbor on file is [[jouvence-blue|Jouvence Blue]], almost the same at 2.9 CIEDE2000 units [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this teal, as photographed, in 17 of 23,781 paintings, 0.07 percent, rarer than 72 percent of the named colors we track [5]. The earliest dated match is a 1515 portrait by Cornelis Engebrechtsz, 397 years before Maerz and Paul's recorded date; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [5].
